lessons.title: Nutrient Requirements of Broilers by Growth Stage
lessons.body: Broilers need different amounts of nutrients as they grow. In the first 10 days (starter phase), chicks need high protein (22-24%) and high energy (3000-3100 kcal/kg) for rapid organ and muscle development. A common mistake is feeding too little protein early, which stunts growth permanently. From day 11 to 24 (grower phase), protein drops to 20-21% and energy stays around 3100 kcal/kg. From day 25 to market (finisher phase), protein drops to 18-19% and energy increases to 3200 kcal/kg to promote fattening. These numbers are for standard commercial broilers like Cobb 500 or Ross 308. If you raise slower-growing local breeds, reduce protein by 1-2%. You must also provide essential amino acids: lysine, methionine, and threonine. Maize and soybean meal are the main ingredients, but they lack enough methionine, so you add synthetic methionine (1-2 kg per tonne of feed). Minerals like calcium and phosphorus are critical for bone growth: starter needs 1% calcium and 0.45% available phosphorus; finisher needs 0.9% calcium and 0.35% phosphorus. Too much calcium in starter causes kidney damage. Vitamins and trace minerals (zinc, iron, copper, manganese, selenium) are added via premix at 0.25-0.5% of the diet. Salt (sodium chloride) at 0.2-0.3% provides sodium and chloride. Always check the feed label or mix your own using a formula from a trusted extension officer. Weigh feed daily and adjust based on bird weight and feed conversion ratio (FCR). A good FCR at market is 1.6-1.8 kg feed per kg live weight. If FCR is above 2.0, your nutrient balance or feed management is off.

lessons.title: Feed Ingredients and Formulation Basics
lessons.body: Formulating broiler feed means mixing energy sources, protein sources, minerals, and additives in correct proportions. In Africa, the cheapest energy source is yellow maize (60-70% of the diet). Other energy sources include sorghum, millet, cassava chips, and wheat bran, but they have lower energy or anti-nutritional factors. For protein, soybean meal (44-48% protein) is best, but it is expensive. You can replace up to 50% of soybean meal with sunflower cake, groundnut cake, or cottonseed cake, but cottonseed has gossypol which is toxic to chicksâlimit to 5% in starter. Fishmeal (60-65% protein) is excellent but costly; use 2-5% in starter only. Animal by-products like blood meal and meat-and-bone meal are risky due to disease and variable quality. Always use a Pearson square or a computer program like WinFeed or FeedSoft to balance nutrients. A simple starter formula (100 kg): maize 55 kg, soybean meal 30 kg, fishmeal 5 kg, wheat bran 5 kg, limestone 1 kg, dicalcium phosphate 1.5 kg, salt 0.3 kg, premix 0.25 kg, methionine 0.15 kg, lysine 0.1 kg, and vegetable oil 1.7 kg. Mix thoroughly for 10 minutes in a horizontal mixer or on a clean concrete floor with a shovel. Never mix on bare groundâyou lose nutrients and introduce pathogens. Test your ingredients for moisture (should be below 12%) and mould before use. Buy from reputable suppliers and keep records of batch numbers. Formulation is not guesswork: use a known formula and adjust only when you have laboratory analysis. If you cannot afford a lab, use book values but be aware of variability. For small flocks, buying ready-made commercial feed is safer and often cheaper than mixing your own.

lessons.title: Feeding Programs: Starter, Grower, Finisher
lessons.body: A feeding program tells you what feed to give, when, and how much. Broilers are usually fed three diets: starter (day 1-10), grower (day 11-24), and finisher (day 25 to market). Starter feed is crumbled or mashed for easy eating. Give chicks unlimited feed (ad libitum) for the first 7 days, but clean feeders twice daily to avoid mouldy leftovers. From day 8 to 10, switch gradually to grower by mixing 50:50 for two days. Grower feed is usually pellets or mash. Continue ad libitum, but monitor feed intake: a healthy broiler eats about 50-60 g/day at 3 weeks. Finisher feed is given from day 25 until sale, often with a withdrawal period of 5-7 days before slaughter if the feed contains medication. Never restrict feed unless directed by a vet; restricted feeding reduces weight gain and extends grow-out. A typical broiler eats 3.5-4.0 kg of feed to reach 2.0-2.5 kg live weight in 35-42 days. If you use local breeds, expect lower weights and longer time. Use feeders that prevent spillage: tube feeders with a lip, or tray feeders for chicks. Provide one feeder per 50 birds for chicks and one per 30 birds for older birds. Adjust feeder height so the lip is at the level of the birds' backs. Clean and disinfect feeders weekly. Water is also part of the program: provide clean water ad libitum, and add electrolytes or vitamins on hot days. Record daily feed consumption and compare with breed standards. If intake drops suddenly, check for disease, heat stress, or feed quality problems. Always keep a feeding chart on the wall of your broiler house.

lessons.title: Feed Presentation and Feeding Management
lessons.body: Feed presentation means the physical form of feed: mash, crumbles, or pellets. Chicks (0-10 days) do best on crumbles because they are easy to pick up and digest. Mash (finely ground) can cause pasting in the beak and waste. Pellets (for grower and finisher) reduce waste and increase intake, but they cost more to produce. If you cannot pellet, use a coarse mashânot powder. Always sift out fine powder before feeding; powder causes respiratory problems and is wasted. Feeding management includes how you distribute feed. For the first 3 days, spread feed on clean paper or tray feeders every 2-3 hours to encourage eating. After day 4, use tube feeders. Fill feeders to one-third capacity to prevent spillage. Feed at the same times daily: early morning and late afternoon are best in hot climates. Never let feeders run empty for more than 2 hours. Remove any wet or mouldy feed immediatelyâit can kill your birds. Provide one feeder per 50 chicks for the first week, then one per 30 birds. Place feeders evenly so all birds can eat at once. Use a feed scoop to measureâdon't guess. A simple rule: 100 broilers at 4 weeks eat about 6 kg of feed per day. Weigh a sample of birds weekly to check growth. If birds are underweight, increase feed access or check for disease. If overweight, reduce energy slightly. Keep a record of feed used per pen. Good feeding management reduces feed waste by 10-15%, which directly increases profit.

lessons.title: Water Quality and Sanitation
lessons.body: Water is the most important nutrient for broilers. A bird can survive days without feed but only hours without water. Broilers drink 1.5 to 2 times as much water as feed by weight. At 30Â°C, a 2 kg broiler drinks about 300 ml per day. Water must be clean, cool (10-20Â°C), and free of pathogens. Never give water from a stagnant pond or dirty well. Test your water source for bacteria (E. coli, Salmonella) and minerals (iron, manganese, nitrate). If you cannot test, treat all water with chlorine at 2-3 ppm (add 1 gram of bleaching powder per 1000 litres, wait 30 minutes). Use a chlorine test kit to confirm. Clean water lines and drinkers daily. For nipple drinkers, flush lines weekly with a 3% hydrogen peroxide solution or commercial line cleaner. For bell drinkers, scrub with a brush and disinfectant, then rinse well. Provide one drinker per 80-100 birds. Place drinkers at the edge of the feeder area, not under feeders. Adjust height so the water level is at the bird's beak. In hot weather, add electrolytes (sodium, potassium, chloride) and vitamin C to water to reduce heat stress. Never add antibiotics to water without veterinary advice. Sanitation also means cleaning feed spills and wet litter, which breed bacteria and flies. Keep a footbath with disinfectant at the entrance of each house. Change footbath daily. Wash hands before entering. If you see diarrhoea or dirty vents, check water quality immediately. Poor water quality reduces feed intake, causes disease, and increases mortality. A simple rule: if you would not drink it, do not give it to your birds.

lessons.title: Feed Storage and Mycotoxin Prevention
lessons.body: Feed storage protects nutrients and prevents mould growth. Store feed in a cool, dry, dark room with good ventilation. Ideal temperature is below 25Â°C and humidity below 65%. Use pallets to keep bags off the floor and 30 cm away from walls. Never store feed on bare concreteâmoisture wicks up. Stack bags no more than 10 high to avoid crushing and heat buildup. Use the first-in, first-out rule: old feed goes out first. Buy only enough feed for 2-3 weeks because vitamins degrade over time. If you mix your own feed, use within 7 days. Mycotoxins are poisons produced by moulds, especially aflatoxin from Aspergillus flavus. They cause liver damage, poor growth, and death. To prevent mycotoxins: buy maize and other ingredients with less than 12% moisture; test with a moisture meter (cost $20-50). Reject any grain with visible mould, discolouration, or musty smell. Store grains in airtight silos or bags with moisture barrier. Add a mould inhibitor like propionic acid (0.5-1 kg per tonne) to finished feed. If you suspect mycotoxins, add a toxin binder (e.g., bentonite clay or yeast cell wall) at 1-2 kg per tonne. Never feed mouldy feedâit is better to discard than to lose your whole flock. Clean storage rooms monthly: sweep, remove old bags, and spray with insecticide to control beetles and weevils. Rodents eat and contaminate feed; set traps and seal holes. Keep a log of feed purchases and storage dates. If you see clumping, caking, or white powder on feed, do not use it.

quiz.q: What is the recommended protein level for broiler starter feed (day 1-10)?
quiz.explanation: Starter feed needs high protein (22-24%) for rapid early growth.

quiz.q: Which amino acid is most often limiting in maize-soybean diets for broilers?
quiz.explanation: Maize is low in methionine, so synthetic methionine is added.

quiz.q: What is the ideal moisture content for feed ingredients to prevent mould?
quiz.explanation: Moisture above 12% encourages mould growth and mycotoxins.

quiz.q: Which feed ingredient is a good plant-based protein source but can contain gossypol?
quiz.explanation: Cottonseed cake contains gossypol, which is toxic to chicks, so limit its use.

quiz.q: In a typical broiler feeding program, when is grower feed given?
quiz.explanation: Grower feed is fed from day 11 to 24, between starter and finisher.

quiz.q: What is the recommended feeder space for broilers older than 3 weeks?
quiz.explanation: Older birds need more feeder space: one tube feeder per 30 birds.

quiz.q: Which feed form is best for day-old chicks?
quiz.explanation: Crumbles are easy for chicks to pick up and digest, reducing waste.

quiz.q: How much water does a 2 kg broiler drink per day at 30Â°C?
quiz.explanation: At 30Â°C, a 2 kg broiler drinks about 300 ml of water daily.

quiz.q: What is the correct chlorine concentration for treating drinking water for broilers?
quiz.explanation: 2-3 ppm chlorine effectively kills pathogens without harming birds.

quiz.q: Which mycotoxin is most common in maize and causes liver damage in broilers?
quiz.explanation: Aflatoxin from Aspergillus flavus is the most dangerous mycotoxin in maize.

quiz.q: What is the recommended calcium level in broiler starter feed?
quiz.explanation: Starter feed needs about 1% calcium for bone development; too much causes kidney damage.

quiz.q: Which of these is a good energy source for broiler feed in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Yellow maize is the cheapest and most common energy source in African broiler diets.

quiz.q: What is the ideal temperature range for storing broiler feed?
quiz.explanation: Cool temperatures below 25Â°C slow nutrient degradation and mould growth.

quiz.q: How many days before slaughter should medicated feed be withdrawn?
quiz.explanation: A 5-7 day withdrawal prevents drug residues in meat.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of adding a toxin binder to feed?
quiz.explanation: Toxin binders like bentonite clay bind mycotoxins so they pass through without harm.

quiz.q: Which factor most reduces feed intake in hot weather?
quiz.explanation: Heat stress reduces feed intake; provide cool water and electrolytes.

quiz.q: What is the recommended mixing time for home-mixed broiler feed?
quiz.explanation: Mixing for 10 minutes ensures uniform distribution of nutrients and additives.

quiz.q: Which of these is a sign of poor water quality in broiler houses?
quiz.explanation: Dirty vents indicate diarrhoea, often caused by contaminated water.

quiz.q: What is the approximate feed conversion ratio (FCR) for a well-managed broiler at market?
quiz.explanation: Good FCR is 1.6-1.8 kg feed per kg live weight; above 2.0 indicates problems.

quiz.q: Which mineral is critical for bone growth and must be balanced with calcium?
quiz.explanation: Available phosphorus must be balanced with calcium for proper bone development.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do if you suspect mycotoxin contamination in feed?
quiz.explanation: Never feed mouldy feed; discarding prevents flock losses.

quiz.q: How often should you clean and disinfect drinkers?
quiz.explanation: Daily cleaning prevents biofilm and pathogen buildup in drinkers.

quiz.q: Which ingredient is a good source of protein but risky due to disease and variable quality?
quiz.explanation: Meat-and-bone meal can carry diseases and has inconsistent nutrient levels.

quiz.q: What is the recommended height for a feeder lip?
quiz.explanation: The feeder lip should be at the level of the birds' backs to reduce spillage.

quiz.q: Which practice helps prevent feed waste?
options: A) Fill feeders to the top
quiz.explanation: Filling feeders one-third full reduces spillage and waste.

quiz.q: What is the ideal relative humidity for feed storage?
quiz.explanation: Humidity below 65% prevents mould growth and caking.

quiz.q: Which vitamin is often added to water to reduce heat stress?
quiz.explanation: Vitamin C helps birds cope with heat stress when added to drinking water.

quiz.q: What is the first-in, first-out rule for feed storage?
quiz.explanation: Using oldest feed first prevents nutrient degradation and spoilage.

quiz.q: Which of these is a sign of good feed quality?
quiz.explanation: Uniform colour and texture indicate well-mixed, fresh feed.

quiz.q: How much water should be provided per 100 birds in a broiler house?
quiz.explanation: Provide one drinker per 80-100 birds to ensure adequate access.
